title: Investigator pocket map: SLI ↔ Trace translation
content:
Purpose:
Short, usable pocket map for oncall/investigators: how to translate a failing SLI into focused trace anchors and a minimal dashboard view that surfaces the root cause quickly. Not a full playbook — meant to be taped to a monitor.

Context / assumptions:
- Multi-tenant token inference system with prefix caching, routing layer (model variants), and KV cache per GPU pool.
- Costy traces: full-trace sampling budget is limited. We must pick anchors carefully.
- SLI failures typically show up as latency regressions, spike in 5xx, or sudden cold-cache effects.

Quick SLI → trace anchor mapping (first-pass):
1) SLI: p95 end-to-end generation latency (user-facing)
   - Immediate trace anchors: routing-decision span, model-invoke span, kv-cache-lookup span, tokenization span.
   - Collect tags: tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, sequence_length_bucket (short/med/long), kv_hit boolean.

2) SLI: tail token-latency (time between token N and N+1)
   - Anchors: kv-cache-eviction span, kv-restore/prefetch span, attention-kernel-switch marker, batching-delay span.
   - Tags: batch_size, kernel_path (int8/fp16), gpu_host, pending_queue_ms.

3) SLI: 5xx rate or model-timeout errors
   - Anchors: model-process crash/oom span, routing-fallback span, retry loop spans.
   - Tags: exception_class, oom? (true/false), fallback_model_variant.

4) SLI: increased token cost (unexpectedly high token output)
   - Anchors: prompt-normalization step, generation-decoding span, function/tool-call spans.
   - Tags: prompt_length, decoding_strategy, heuristics_applied.

Trace capture rules (practical):
- All traces for alerts: sample 100% for first 5 minutes after a new alert fires, then ramp down to stratified sampling: 10% of normal sessions + 50% of sessions with kv_hit=false + 25% of sessions where sequence_length_bucket=long.
- Mandatory metadata on every sampled span: tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, kernel_path, trace_id, span_id. Keep these indexable.
- Avoid PII: redact user prompt text in traces; keep only prompt hash + token_count.

Dashboard minimal investigator view (3 tiles to surface root cause):
1) Triage ribbon (left):
   - p50/p95/p99 latency (end-to-end) by tenant cohort & route (small multiples)
   - 5xx rate and recent deploy markers
   - KV-hit ratio over time (5m window)
2) Anchor heatmap (center):
   - Median duration by span type (routing, kv-lookup, model-invoke, batching) stacked by model_variant
   - Highlight sudden deltas vs baseline (7d baseline)
3) Session sample panel (right):
   - List of recent sampled traces (clickable): time, tenant, route, kv_hit, sequence_length_bucket, root-span-duration
   - Quick-replay link to prompt-replay harness (if allowed)

Widget heuristics and cost controls:
- Default dashboard shows aggregated data for top-20 tenants; provide tenant-picker for ad-hoc deep-dive.
- Use pre-aggregated rollups for p95 to reduce query cost; show raw quantiles only for drill-down.
- Limit auto-refresh to 30s for operator pages; 5s only for active incident UI.

Run-from-alert rapid checklist (short):
1) Confirm alert signal: which SLI and which percentiles.
2) Check deploy timeline: any model/artifact/infra deploy in last 15m.
3) Open triage ribbon: is kv_hit ratio dropping? routing latency spiking?
4) If kv_hit low -> look at eviction metrics and prefetch failures; check particle logs for eviction storms.
5) If model-invoke dominates -> inspect GPU host-level metrics (gpu_util, cuda-mem), kernel_path mix, retry/oom tags.
6) Capture 20 full traces (if available) with full span context and save to incident bucket.
7) Postmortem stub: note root cause hypothesis and signal to add to SLO dashboard if recurring.

Sampling budget mini-calculator (for incident window):
- Budget = max_trace_rate_per_minute (configured) * incident_minutes.
- If budget < needed_traces, prioritize by: tenant_weight (customer priority) > kv_hit=false > long-sequence.

Operational notes for instrumentation owners:
- New spans must be cheap: include only essential numeric fields and short tags. No raw prompts.
- Add a "trace_anchor" tag to spans that should persist across sampling (routing, kv-lookup, model-invoke). This helps re-assembly when traces are partial.
- Use consistent tag names across services: tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, kernel_path, kv_hit. Anti-pattern: mixing route_id and routeName.

Dashboard UX suggestions (investigator-focused):
- Provide a small explanation overlay per tile: what it surfaces and when it lies.
- Default dashboard should answer "Is this infrastructure, model, or data?" in top-left.
- Provide a fast toggle: aggregate vs per-tenant view (persist selection in URL).

Open questions / follow-ups (actions):
- [ ] Define explicit tenant priority weights for trace sampling (JIRA-OBS-4201).
- [ ] Add trace_anchor tag to serving-router & kv layer (owner: Marco).
- [ ] Evaluate storing prompt hashes in trace index for faster repro (privacy review required).
- [ ] Mock incident drill with synthetic low kv_hit scenario and confirm dashboards surface cause within 5 minutes.

Notes to self / shorthand: 
- When seeing p95 spike, check kv_hit first (most common), then kernel_path switching (e.g., when quantized kernel is chosen, token tails can spike).
- Watch out for tenant-specific cold-start patterns: repeated low-volume tenants can have warmup thrashing.

References & shortcuts:
- SLI taxonomy: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/SLI+Taxonomy
- Trace retention & costs: JIRA-OBS-4018
- Dashboard repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-dashboards/pull/78

If you're oncall and this doc helped, add a one-liner to the notes section on the dashboard. Will iterate after next incident.
